title: Headlines, Framing, and Unspoken Assumptions
text:
Headlines are designed to capture attention within seconds, and their wording often carries more interpretive weight than the article beneath them. A headline that describes a policy as 'a betrayal' signals an evaluation before any evidence has been presented. Readers who skim only the headline therefore absorb a judgement they never consciously accepted.

Discourse analysts argue that such framing operates through presupposition rather than assertion. When a report refers to 'so-called experts' or 'a controversial bill', it presupposes a disagreement that the text may not have demonstrated. Media literacy, on this view, means recognising which claims are stated openly and which are quietly assumed.

questions.text: What does the first paragraph say headlines are designed to do?
According to the second paragraph, how does framing operate?
options: Through the length of the article

questions.text: What does the passage imply about readers who only skim headlines?
options: They may absorb judgements they never consciously accepted
They always read the full article

questions.text: Why might phrases such as 'so-called experts' be significant?
options: They prove that the experts are unqualified
They presuppose a disagreement the text may not have shown
They are a neutral description of the people quoted
They are required by law in all reporting

vocabulary.definition: the short, prominent lines that introduce a news story
the way an issue is presented so as to shape how it is understood
something taken for granted in a statement without being explicitly asserted
an opinion or evaluation formed about something

paragraph_translations: Los titulares están diseñados para captar la atención en segundos, y su redacción suele tener más peso interpretativo que el artículo que sigue. Un titular que describe una política como «una traición» anuncia una valoración antes de que se presente ninguna prueba. Por eso, quienes solo hojean el titular absorben un juicio que nunca aceptaron conscientemente.

Los analistas del discurso sostienen que ese encuadre opera mediante la presuposición y no mediante la afirmación. Cuando un informe se refiere a «los llamados expertos» o a «un proyecto de ley polémico», presupone un desacuerdo que el texto quizá no ha demostrado. Desde este punto de vista, la alfabetización mediática consiste en reconocer qué afirmaciones se formulan abiertamente y cuáles se asumen en silencio.
